title: Intelligence artificielle / intelligence humaine : qui contrôle qui ?

bias_targets.methodology: Literature review and conceptual analysis of human heuristics affecting decision-making, specifically focusing on optimism bias, in-group bias, confirmation bias, and representativeness bias.

Literature review citing existing empirical studies, such as the evaluation of equivalent CVs with male versus female names and algorithmic discrimination in assigning higher loan interest rates to women.

Literature review highlighting algorithmic discrimination in financial algorithms, specifically the use of proxy variables leading to disproportionate subprime loan offers to African-American and Hispanic borrowers.
Review of experimental research (e.g., the trolley problem scenarios) demonstrating human prejudice and skepticism toward moral justifications when they are attributed to an AI rather than a human.
